gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.

gaps.sentence: The medicine had an immediate ___ on her breathing.
gaps.explanation: 'An effect on' — the noun form is required here.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of service, she is one of our most ___ employees.
gaps.explanation: 'A valued member/employee' is someone the organisation appreciates; 'valuable' stresses monetary or practical worth.

gaps.sentence: She gave me some useful ___ about buying a house.
gaps.hint: a noun is needed after 'some useful'
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the uncountable noun; 'advise' is the verb. 'Advices' is not standard English.

gaps.sentence: The ___ of repairing the roof was higher than we expected.
gaps.hint: the amount of money needed to do something
gaps.explanation: 'The cost of doing something' is the money needed to do it; 'price' is asked for goods, not activities.

gaps.sentence: We ___ all major credit cards at the box office.
gaps.explanation: 'Accept' means to take or agree to something offered; 'except' means not including.
'Complement' means to combine well with or complete something; 'compliment' means to praise.
